presentation._comment_shadow_opacity: Stormwood's scene authors a 0.68 canopy-shadow floor for its permanent storm. WorldLook reapplies the global sun defaults after scene setup, so every phase must carry that realm-local value explicitly; Break alone returns to fully hard shadows, as the surge brief specifies.
presentation._comment_phases: F10 phase readability (WORLD 5.2, ART_DIRECTION 3.3/4, AUDIO 4.3). Each phase is nameable without HUD text from sky, light, rain and flash: Calm = soft grey-green overcast, drizzle; Building = heavier, darker, faster-moving copper-tinged ceiling, rain thickening, no strike; Break = darkest violet-slate ceiling, full rain, white-violet flash rhythm; Fading = thinning ceiling, warm afterglow horizon, rain easing. sky_* and ceiling_colour are daylight values; stormwood_surge.gd scales them once by the live sky's luminance (night_scale, floor night_scale_floor) before any cross-fade, and dims ambient_colour toward the native ambient's value as night falls, so the storm never brightens the night. Building and Break cool/dim ambient and lower the sun so the ground answers the dark sky (visual judge J2). fog_colour always follows sky_horizon (art.json's fog/horizon seam rule). No red: oxblood is Team Tether's.
presentation._comment_reapply: WorldLook re-merges its whole look per set_weather call, so the weather layer is re-applied every reapply_fading_seconds during a cross-fade and every reapply_steady_seconds otherwise (to follow the day clock). The ceiling updates every frame.
presentation._comment_floors: Review R2-2 / round-2 judge (a),(b): the storm horizon (and fog, which equals it) never falls below horizon_fraction of the native horizon luminance for the hour, and the ceiling never below ceiling_fraction of it, keeping each phase's authored hue. Night Break stays violet-indigo instead of sinking to black; day Break's sky reads as a storm afternoon, not night. Ceilings are fully opaque (no sun/moon ghost through them); only Fading's breakup opens gaps, and only by day.
presentation._comment_rain: Stormwood's own rain emitter (world_weather.gd builds it hidden and Meadows-sized). max_drops is the Break (amount 1.0) count; each phase's rain_amount scales it. wind_slant tilts the fall (x, z per unit of fall) and streaks align to their velocity. A slanted drop drifts about 3 m over its life, so each emission ring is shifted upwind by upwind_offset_fraction of that drift, and the near ring's inner radius keeps every drop at least 1.5 m from the camera at the longest arm (riding, 6.8 m + margin), which a unit test computes (the R5.2 near-lens streak defect). far_layer is shorter and fainter (depth fade). At night the tint follows the night factor down to night_floor and alpha drops to night_alpha_fraction.
presentation._comment_telegraph: The strike warning uses the game's one hazard colour, read at runtime from combat.json telegraph.colour (magenta; see its _why_colour_0905: white-violet read as a heal/selection circle and amber as reward gold, here as in combat). Rim exactly at strike.radius_m, a glow of the same colour for edge_falloff_m past it, a dark interior (fill_colour) that darkens the ground as the strike nears, a pulse chirping pulse_hz_start->pulse_hz_end over strike.telegraph_seconds, and a white-hot core on impact. Only the rim and glow are pulled depth_pull_m (about grass height) toward the camera, never the fill, so the fill cannot draw over a trainer at the near rim. One cached indexed mesh; per strike only the centre and 16 rim heights are sampled.
presentation._comment_aftermath: After the Long Storm (stormwood:long_storm_ended) WORLD 5.2 says the sky opens and Breaks become rare; ART_DIRECTION: 'after release, sky and ordinary forest colour return without erasing scars'. The aftermath Calm (2400 s) therefore drops every storm override: null sky/ambient colours leave art.json's own time-of-day sky and ambient, the ceiling is fully open, no rain, full sun. The short aftermath Building/Break/Fading keep the storm rows (a real storm still passes) with these lighter overrides.
presentation._comment_flash: Break's flash rhythm (ART_DIRECTION 3.3 'flash rhythm', 4 'white-violet lightning'). Distant flashes on their own 4-8 s timer (WORLD 5.2's strike spacing) light the ceiling and add a brief white-violet directional light. A strike impact always draws its bolt and local light at the impact; its whole-sky flash is full only while the local presentation is Break, otherwise it fades with distance from the local player to zero at strike_sky_range_m (glass-sink strikes happen in any phase and are broadcast to every peer). strike_* are the impact's bolt and light in stormwood_lightning.gd.

strike._why_spare_trainer_in_fight: Coordinator interim ruling 2026-09-25 (WO-F11-04, pending owner decision): while a trainer is committed to a creature fight, strikes do not target the trainer's position; they may still land as telegraphed hazards at the piloted creature, and strikes resume on the trainer when the fight ends. Host-authoritative and per peer. The earned witness measured 6 of 6 strikes on a trainer standing through one road fight (100 -> 0 health), because the stick drives the creature, not the trainer, during combat.
